name: Nudd
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Nudd, also called Lludd, is a British god. In the Roman period a large shrine stood for a god named Nodens. Scholars believe Nodens is the same being as the Welsh Nudd or Lludd. Nudd appears surrounded by tritons, the symbols of the sea. From the temple's position and this imagery he reads as god of the river's mouth or estuary, and perhaps of the headlands. In Welsh myth Nudd, more commonly Lludd, ruled Britain. He was brother of the Continental king Llefelys. He built London. First demons swept across the country, then came two dragons, then a giant magician. With help from his brother, Nudd beat every one of these plagues.

okr.objective: Nudd is a British god who ruled Britain and built London.
key_results: A Roman-era temple honored a god called Nodens, held to be Nudd or Lludd.
From the tritons around him, Nudd is read as god of the river mouth and estuary.
Nudd ruled Britain and was brother of the Continental king Llefelys.
He built London and, with his brother, conquered the plagues that struck it.
